label: DoS Hulk
rationale: T1499.002 describes a simple HTTP flood that overwhelms a web server; Hulk is an HTTP request flood.

label: DoS GoldenEye
rationale: T1499.002 covers HTTP floods against web services; GoldenEye is an HTTP flood with keep-alive.

label: DoS slowloris
rationale: Slow HTTP connections exhaust server resources (T1499). Parent technique used because the definitions do not separate slow-connection attacks from flood attacks.

label: DoS Slowhttptest
rationale: Slow HTTP requests exhaust server resources (T1499). Parent technique used for the same reason as slowloris.

label: DDoS
rationale: T1498.001 describes a high-volume direct network flood sent by one or more systems at a target.

label: PortScan
rationale: Probing ports and services to discover which are reachable (Network Service Discovery).

label: FTP-Patator
rationale: T1110.001 describes systematic password guessing against a login.

label: SSH-Patator
rationale: T1110.001 describes systematic password guessing against a login.

label: Bot
rationale: T1071.001 describes C2 traffic embedded in web protocols; the dataset's bot polls over HTTP.

label: Web Attack - Brute Force
rationale: Repeated login attempts against a web application (password guessing).

label: Web Attack - XSS
rationale: T1190 covers exploiting a weakness in an Internet-facing web application; the XSS flaw is the weakness exploited.

label: Web Attack - XSS
rationale: T1189 (Drive-by Compromise) names cross-site scripting explicitly as a way to insert malicious scripts through web application interfaces, which is the XSS payload's effect on the victim's browser.

label: Web Attack - Sql Injection
rationale: T1190 explicitly lists databases and web applications as exploitable public-facing systems; SQL injection is such an exploit.

label: Heartbleed
rationale: Exploitation of an Internet-facing TLS service (CVE-2014-0160) is a software-weakness exploit covered by T1190.

label: Infiltration
rationale: CIC-IDS2017 describes Infiltration as an exploit followed by backdoor activity. No single ATT&CK technique matches that end-to-end sequence, so no technique is assigned.
